trajectory_summary: The call opens with mild friction over lead staleness and a disclosed prior negative solar experience, but the rep holds a steady verification cadence and the customer actively cooperates through a lengthy, effortful bill-retrieval process. The call ends with a locked appointment day and time, showing energy built across the call despite a rough open.

observed_outcome.quote: Yeah. Looks like we could do would eleven or twelve work better for you?
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day (tomorrow) and time (twelve) were locked, a callback number was collected and read back for confirmation, and the rep confirmed email access for the design — this is a fully booked phone appointment. The co-owner (wife) was identified on title but never invited or confirmed for the call, so co_owner_confirmed is false.

bill_anchor_audit.bill_quote: So March to April, I used a 172 kilowatts per hour.
bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep captured twelve full months of kWh usage data (04:41-06:12) but never turned any of it into an emotional or curiosity-driven reason to act — the flip should have landed around 06:12 when the rep says 'That's exactly what we're looking for,' which could easily have included a reflection of the winter usage spike instead of a generic close. Note also that the schema's separate verify.average_bill dollar-figure item was never actually answered — the customer supplied kWh usage only, never a monthly dollar amount, which is a distinct minor gap from the usage-history capture.

bill_document_audit.ask_quote: I also need that usage history. So that's great you're pulling up.
bill_document_audit.result_quote: Yeah. I have here from May 2025 to April 2026.
bill_document_audit.reasoning: The rep asked for usage history and the customer logged into his Dominion Energy online account live on the call, then read off twelve months of kWh figures verbally — a read-aloud from an online login rather than a photo or document send, fully satisfying the bill-document requirement despite taking several minutes of login friction.

interest_reason_audit.reason_quote: Yes. So I don't have to get the electric bill every month, or at least I can get a lower electric bill every month.
interest_reason_audit.reasoning: Customer clearly states the motivation is reducing/eliminating the electric bill, but the rep never ties this reason back into the close or the scheduling pitch — the appointment-setting language at 06:12 is generic and doesn't reference the bill-reduction goal the customer named.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: bill/usage anchor never flipped into curiosity or urgency
primary_coaching_focus.why: The rep captured an unusually rich, high-variance twelve-month usage history — exactly the raw material the schema calls the setter's primary anchor — but filed it silently and moved straight to scheduling without reflecting a single number back to the customer. This is the single largest missed leverage point on the call.

key_moments.quote: Oh, looks like we've we've been speaking to you a couple days ago.
key_moments.stewart_read: The rep acknowledges the record mismatch but doesn't resolve it — customer says the request was actually a month old, a discrepancy the rep never investigates (recycled lead misfiled as fresh?). The call moves on without correcting the record or probing why the timing is off.

key_moments.quote: I have I have received it, like, before, but, I don't know. It didn't convince me.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer discloses a prior solar design that failed to convince him. The rep asks when ("two or three years ago") but never asks WHAT wasn't convincing — price, savings numbers, company, panel type. This is exactly the competitive intel a closer would want.

key_moments.quote: In order to qualify for the current programs, all we ask of the homeowner is you just have a credit score of at least 670.
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep states the credit threshold correctly at 670, matching the schema (unlike the 650 drift seen in other calls) and times the question efficiently while the customer is occupied pulling up his utility account.

key_moments.quote: Is there anybody else with title with you, or is it just My wife. Your wife.
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep correctly identifies a co-owner (wife) on title but never returns to this fact when booking the appointment — the appointment is set with only Enrique's phone number, no mention of including his wife on the closer call.
